text:
elaine: Heads-up: proposal for a compact-slab allocator prototype for Dedicated GPU pools. Goal: reduce wasted slot capacity by issuing small "slab" leases (1/4 or 1/8 GPU) that the allocator packs into physical leases. Wanted quick feedback on API shape, operator boundary, and safety.

jordy: Interesting. How are slabs represented to the runtime? Do we need kernel/runtime changes for memory isolation?

elaine: We expose logical slab namespaces to runtime so KV cache keys and process-level quotas are namespaced. No kernel changes. The runtime adapter enforces per-slab memory quotas and maps logical namespaces to physical process allocations.

kai: Major risks: noisy-neighbor memory pressure and tail latency when many slabs share one card. How do we prevent a single tenant from monopolizing many slabs on a single GPU?

elaine: We'll enforce per-tenant slab caps and prefer spread packing across nodes. Also admit API returns throttle hints and an eviction_priority hint so runtime can degrade low-priority work first.

nina: Operator boundary should be minimal: operator manages only physical leases and reported capacity. Allocator sends intent documents (desired GPU counts and labels) periodically; operator reconciler does not need per-slab state.

jordy: Persistence and recovery? Allocator crash shouldn't lose slab manifests or double-allocate.
